items.t: St. Marys River Sea Lamprey Trap (SLT)
items.d: THIS IS A PRE-SOLCITATION NOTICE. THIS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL OR INVITATION FOR BID. The US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Detroit District is seeking contractors with the capability to provide construction services for the St. Marys River Sea Lamprey Trap (SLT) project. This project consists of construction of a sea lamprey trap structure downstream of Gate 16 of the St. Marys River Compensating Works in Chippewa County, MI. The project will involve installing a steel grating platform, trap vault, and lift system. The steel-grating platform will be 11-feet-long and 8-feet-wide and be supported by steel members fixed to a concrete wingwall. The trap vault will be composed of steel plates and fixed to the required platform and the existing concrete sill. The lift system will include one free-standing jib crane with a minimum rating of 1 ton. Demobilize when complete. NO SOLICITATION,

items.t: Post Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Readiness and Validation Status
items.d: https://feedback.gsa.gov/jfe/form/SV_3t6dNlgkS4Vg6iy Federal agencies are preparing for the transition from cryptographic algorithms that may be vulnerable to future quantum computing attacks to quantum-resistant cryptographic algorithms standardized by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). Public key cryptographic algorithms (i.e. asymmetric cryptography) currently used across Federal information systems, products and services — including Rivest-Shamir-Adleman (RSA), elliptic curve Diffie-Hellman(ECDH), elliptic curve digital signature algorithms (ECDSA), and related mechanisms — will be vulnerable to a future cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer (CRQC). As a result, Federal agencies are expected to identify, prioritize, and migrate quantum-vulnerable cryptographic systems to approved post-quantum cryptographic algorithms. Through this project, several recreation areas will be decommissioned in the Tonto Basin Ranger District (RD), and Globe RD. The decommission of campgrounds at the Tonto Bassin RD is the base bid and at Globe RD, it is an option bid. The intent of this work is to remove and safely dispose outside of the National Forest boundaries, recreational accommodations that include but not limited to Entry station buildings, toilets buildings, sidewalks, asphalt pavement, fish cleaning stations, septic system, and parking lots.

items.d: PROJECT NUMBER: UT NP ARCH 100(2) PROJECT NAME: Bridges on Delicate Arch Road PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Delicate Arch Road (DAR) is within Arches National Park (Park) and provides access to Delicate Arch. DAR is a functional class 1 roadway (Principal Park Road) and is heavily traveled by visitors and often congested during periods with moderate-to-high levels of visitation. DAR crosses three low-gradient ephemeral washes (Salt Valley Wash, Salt Wash, and Winter Camp Wash) near their confluence in the Salt Wash Basin downstream of Wolfe Ranch. Culverts installed during original road construction in the mid-1990s and during subsequent upgrades are inadequate to allow unobstructed stream flow and sediment transport downstream. items.d: The scope of this SATOC is to provide services to prepare and facilitate group partnering workshops and to train government personnel to develop organic expertise to plan and facilitate informal team led partnering sessions. Professionally facilitated and formal partnering is an integral element of the USACE project governance process. To accomplish USACE construction contracts most effectively, the Government requires the formation of a cohesive and collaborative partnership within the project team with the common goal of drawing on the strength of each organization in an effort to achieve a successful project without safety mishaps, conforming to the contract, within budget and on schedule. The effort will be to assist (facilitate) teams in developing processes, procedures, and methods for measuring and sustaining team performance and accountability throughout the life of a project.

items.t: Lower Brule North Shoreline Stabilization And Ecosystem Restoration, Element 2
items.d: The project is located along the right descending bank of Lake Sharpe near the Lower Brule, SD town site. Lower Brule North Element 2 includes a 100-foot-wide riparian planting bench, a gravel maintenance path along the entire reach, a riprap revetment to protect the shoreline and island from erosion, and the creation of a 200-by-1,500-foot island constructed in water up to three feet deep. The sheltered open water area between the island and the shoreline will develop into approximately 5.17 acres of emergent wetland, and this will also create approximately 32 acres of riparian habitat. Related tasks include earth moving, grading, bank shaping, rock installation, water management, fill, and topsoil placement.

items.t: RF Roof Replacement Project
items.d: The Princeton Plasmas Physics Laboratory is seeking a qualified contractor to replace roofing on two existing roofs. The (C40 RF Building & C41 CS Building) which are past their useful life requiring costly maintenance to upkeep. Severe water infiltration occurs regularly at failing joints, punctures, and flashing. Portions of existing metal coping have pulled away during storm events causing large sections of membrane to separate from the substrate. A catastrophic failure to one of these roofs would negatively impact the ability to conduct the top priority experimental operations in the Laboratory. The Subcontractor shall provide all materials, labor, supervision, equipment, and expertise required to replace the noted roofs and specified components per the associated contractdesign documents. Construction scope includes the following: Remove and replace existing built-up roofs at PPPL.

items.t: Air Force Contract Augmentation Program (AFCAP) VI
items.d: The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS/PKD) is issuing this solicitation for the Air Force Contract Augmentation Program VI (AFCAP VI). This is a Multiple-Award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract designed to provide rapid, global contingency planning, logistics, and emergency construction capabilities to the Department of the Air Force, other DoD components, and Federal agencies. The AFCAP serves as a responsive, global force multiplier for commanders and Government agencies, supporting contingencies both within the contiguous United States (CONUS) and outside the contiguous United States (OCONUS).The AFCAP supports United States (U.S.) national interests and security objectives by providing rapid-response capabilities for contingency planning, deployment, training/equipping of forces, emergency/contingency construction, logistics/commodities, and services.

items.t: Borough of Millvale, Pennsylvania, Local Protection Project (LPP) PL84-99 Rehabilitation
items.d: The Millvale LPP was constructed by U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) in 1980 under the authority of Section 205 of the Flood Control Act of 1948 as amended. The project consists of about 6,200 feet of channel improvement including concrete gravity retaining walls, concrete wall supports, anchored concrete toe blocks, concrete cap walls, stone-filled gabion mattresses, flap gates and access ramps. The LPP is an urban Flood Control Work (FCW), and it is not a multipurpose project. Heavy rains from 1-12 April 2024 caused flooding which damaged the Project within Girtys Run, including bank erosion, shoaling, erosion of the improved channel, ruptured gabion baskets, washed-out concrete buttresses, and erosion of grouted riprap. items.d: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Tulsa District has been tasked to solicit for and award a contract for providing and installing two new 8-inch station service draft tube drain gate valves and two new 16-inch unwatering gate valves at Denison Dam Powerhouse. items.t: SNPLMA Kalamazoo Fence
items.d: This intent of this project is to construct approximately 0.5 miles of barbwire fence lines near Kalamazoo Campground on the Ely Ranger District. Construct two barbwire drift fences totaling approximately 0.5 miles in length to exclude active grazing within Kalamazoo Campground. Livestock in the campground presents a safety hazard and has resulted in numerous complaints from the public. In addition, limiting livestock activities within the campground will also extend protection of newly installed recreational infrastructure. This project includes construction of approximately 2,500 feet of new barbwire fence including installation of an estimated four 12-foot wire gates as a lump sum.

items.t: Rosebud Lift Station Construction
items.d: The existing lift station has been in place since the early 1990s. Since its creation the hospital anticipates increased expansion in the emergency department, added on Tribal programs (dialysis, detox, Tribal Health Administration Building), added on 19 more quarters units, and is anticipating adding an additional 23 quarters units. The existing pumps are facing replacement every 1-2 years due to the unanticipated growth, but due to the growth we need to consider increasing the capacity of the wet well. In addition to switching from standard submersible pumps to chopper pumps to accommodate the random objects that get flushed into the system. In July both pumps ended up failing and they had to not only replace the pumps but pay for sewage disposal to circumvent overflow. A separate project is in the works to begin remediating/replacing damaged sewer mains due to inflow and infiltration.

The Mission & Installation Contracting Command (MICC), Fort Drum, NY is seeking multiple businesses willing to enter into a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for services under North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) 561321: Security Systems Services index Fire alarm sales combined with installation, repair, or monitoring services. The small business size standard for this industry is $22.0 million in average annual revenue.
